Cue-task macBP gamma & event-locked spectrograms

Zelano Lab — cueTask analysis

2026-06-30

1. Methods

Data. Cue-task intracranial/scalp recordings, preprocessed to 500 Hz (high-pass 0.03 Hz, low-pass ~Nyquist, notch 60/120/180 Hz). Analysis channels are the bipolar macro pairs macBP1..5 (count varies; sessions without any macBP are excluded). Sessions are grouped as DupiS1 / DupiS2 / DupiS3 (Dupi study, recording session 1/2/3) and Control (all non-Dupi cue sessions).

FOOOF (Task 1). Per session, each macBP PSD (FieldTrip ft_freqanalysis, mtmfft, 2 s segments, 50% overlap, piped in via EEGLAB eeglab2fieldtrip) was parameterized with FOOOF over 2–58 Hz with a knee aperiodic term (cfg.output = fooof_aperiodic / fooof_peaks; brainstorm process_fooof). (The knee + restricted 2–58 Hz range follows the low-frequency 1/f bend; an earlier 2–120 Hz fixed-aperiodic fit mis-modeled the 1/f and inflated apparent gamma-peak heights.) The gamma band is 30–58 Hz. Before selecting bestMac, each channel’s trial-rejection rate is estimated (fraction of trialStart epochs flagged as noisy by the relative sharp-deflection rule, below); channels where this rate exceeds 30% are excluded from bestMac consideration, preventing a high-noise channel whose broadband artifact mimics a gamma peak from being selected. Among the remaining (clean) channels: bestMac is the channel with the largest periodic (oscillatory) gamma peak; if no clean macBP channel has a fitted gamma peak we fall back to the largest flattened (PSD ÷ aperiodic) power; if all channels exceed the 30% threshold we select the least-noisy one (selectionMethod = 'allNoisy_leastBad'). The selectionMethod and per-channel rejRate columns record the outcome.

Spectrograms (Tasks 1–4, z-score method). For each session’s bestMac, per-trial time-frequency power was obtained from EEGLAB newtimef (Morlet, 100 log-spaced freqs 2–120 Hz; single-trial alltfX → |·|²), locked to trialStart and to finalOnset (finalOnset is ~6 s after trialStart). Power was normalized with a bootstrap permutation z-score (myChanZscore): per frequency, a 1000-sample bootstrap distribution of the −700…−200 ms trialStart baseline mean defines the z reference. The finalOnset epoch is z-scored against the same trialStart baseline (its baseline frames are appended before z-scoring), so the two lockings share one scale (heat = z vs baseline).

Noise rejection (relative sharp-deflection rule). Sharp deflections are detected relative to each channel’s own variability, so that a uniformly high-amplitude channel is not rejected merely for being high-amplitude. For the bestMac trace we compute the sliding 10 ms max-to-min range d and robust-z it over the whole recording: zd = (d − median(d)) / (1.4826·MAD(d)) — i.e. how many robust-SDs a given 10 ms swing sits above that channel’s typical 10 ms swing. A 10 ms window is an event if zd > K, and a trial (trialStart-locked epoch −1.75…+5.75 s) is flagged noisy if it contains any event. The threshold K = 10 was calibrated once across the whole dataset (cue_calibrate_noise): it drops 8.1 % of trials overall (>0 % and well under the 20 % budget), with the worst single session losing 75 % and no session fully excluded. The same K applies to every session. (This replaces the earlier absolute >80 µV / 10 ms rule, which scaled with raw amplitude and rejected high-amplitude-but-clean channels wholesale. The noise-aware channel selection (§1) further ensures that a noisy channel cannot be chosen as bestMac — e.g. 240923_OBE_NMH_HRM macBP5 (>80 % trial rejection) is excluded from eligibility and macBP2, which is clean, is selected instead.) Noisy trials are drawn in red on singleTrialRawMac.png and excluded from all spectrograms. The mean respiration trace (chosen rsp channel, flipped) is overlaid on every spectrogram (black line, right axis). Display window −1000…+3000 ms. Group means (Task 4) average the per-subject z maps (and respiration) within each group on one shared color scale.

6. Time-resolved gamma (FOOOF over epochs)

Methods. For each session’s bestMac, Morlet power (2–58 Hz, 100 linear freqs) was computed on the noise-clean finalOnset-locked trials, then averaged over trials and into ten sequential 250 ms windows spanning −500…+2000 ms. FOOOF (same settings as the overall channel fit) was applied to each window’s power spectrum; the largest 30–58 Hz periodic peak per window is recorded in cueTask_gammaEpochs.csv. “Channel-centered” = each window’s gamma peak frequency minus that channel’s overall gamma peak (from §3).

6.5 Does gamma frequency track gamma power across epochs?

Each epoch’s gamma peak is expressed relative to the channel’s whole-recording (overall) FOOOF peak (§3), by subtraction — the appropriate operation given the metrics:

  • Δ frequency = epoch peak − overall peak (Hz). Subtraction (not a ratio) because frequency is interval-scaled; this also removes each individual’s characteristic gamma frequency.
  • Δ power = epoch peak height − overall peak height. gammaPeakPower is the FOOOF peak height above the 1/f aperiodic (log10 power), so it is already aperiodic-/SNR-corrected and its differences are ≈ dB changes; subtracting log-heights is the natural “change.”

Using the overall peak as the reference (rather than the first epoch) is more stable and keeps every epoch informative. (Δpower is mostly negative because a single 250 ms Morlet window has a lower FOOOF peak height than the whole-recording reference fit — a per-session offset that does not affect the within-session slope.) Dots are session×epoch, colored by epoch (ochre→purple), faceted by group. The grey line is a simple pooled linear fit (shown for orientation only); the table below is the proper within-session test — note these can disagree, since a pooled fit mixes within- and between-session variance.

Within-session coupling via a linear mixed-effects model Δfreq ~ Δpower + (Δpower|session), fit per group (random slope; falls back to random intercept if the slope variance is singular). The slope is the within-session change in gamma frequency (Hz) per unit change in gamma power (log10).

Within-session LME: Δfreq ~ Δpower + (Δpower|session), per group.
